Consult Summary:
- Adult female with 2 days of gradual-onset, constant, worsening suprapubic (below umbilicus) burning pain, subjective hot/sweaty, urinary frequency, and pink urine (possible hematuria); mild nausea, no vomiting or dysuria. Empirically treated for presumed acute uncomplicated cystitis; pregnancy test advised; safety-net provided.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Lower abdominal (suprapubic) pain with feeling hot/sweaty.
- Symptom details:
  - Onset/duration: Began ~2 days ago.
  - Character: Burning pain, localized just below the umbilicus; tender on pressure; no radiation.
  - Course: Gradual onset; constant; getting worse but patient remains able to function.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Urinary: Increased frequency; urine “pink” in color (possible hematuria). No dysuria/stinging. Passing urine otherwise OK.
  - GI: Mild nausea; no vomiting. Constipation last week now resolved; bowel movements now normal. No diarrhea.
  - Constitutional: Feels hot and sweaty; no measured temperature.
  - Respiratory/cardiac/neuro: Denies SOB, cough, palpitations, headaches, or vision changes.
- Gynecologic/sexual:
  - Sexually active with one partner; last intercourse ~4 days ago.
  - Contraception: Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) inserted ~1 year ago; still having periods.
  - LMP: ~2 weeks ago (patient also stated “about three weeks ago,” then “two weeks ago”).
  - Last STI screen ~6 months ago, reportedly normal.
  - No vaginal bleeding or discharge mentioned.
- Pertinent negatives: No prior similar episodes.

Past Medical History:
- Generally well; no prior surgeries reported.
- No prior episodes of similar abdominal/urinary symptoms.
- Medications: Implanon (dose/route/frequency as contraceptive implant; insertion ~1 year ago).
- Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
- Lives in a shared house with two roommates.
- Occupation: Accountant.
- Tobacco: Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Social use; no excess reported.
- Other substances: Not documented.

Family History:
- Non-contributory per patient; no relevant bowel/urinary history reported.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Exam findings: Not documented.

Investigations:
- None performed at this visit.
- Pregnancy test: Recommended by clinician (to be done by patient).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected acute uncomplicated cystitis (primary working diagnosis)
  - Rationale: Suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, and pink urine suggest hematuria; mild systemic symptoms; dysuria absent but not required.
  - Plan:
    - Start antibiotics: Trimethoprim. Dosing stated as “two tablets, one tablet twice a day for three days” (conflict noted). Clarify exact dose with prescriber/pharmacy. Prescription sent to patient’s pharmacy.
    - Symptomatic care: Paracetamol/acetaminophen for pain (dose/route/frequency not documented); maintain adequate oral hydration.
    - Additional advice: Cranberry juice may help with urinary symptoms (as advised by clinician).
    - Follow-up: Return/contact clinic in a few days if no improvement; sooner if worsening.
    - Red flags/safety net: Seek urgent care for worsening abdominal pain, persistent high fevers/rigors, vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, flank pain, or feeling very unwell.
- Issue 2: Possible hematuria; rule out other causes (e.g., urolithiasis)
  - Rationale: Report of pink urine; frequency and suprapubic pain could also be seen with distal stone; no flank pain or colicky pattern.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor with current management.
    - If hematuria persists or pain pattern changes (e.g., severe/colicky, flank-to-groin radiation), consider urinalysis and further evaluation (e.g., imaging) at follow-up.
- Issue 3: Pregnancy status unknown; rule out early pregnancy-related complications
  - Rationale: Reproductive age, sexually active, no barrier method; on implant (lower risk) with LMP ~2 weeks ago.
  - Plan:
    - Perform pregnancy test as advised.
    - If positive or if pelvic pain worsens or is associated with vaginal bleeding, dizziness/syncope, or shoulder tip pain, seek urgent evaluation to exclude ectopic pregnancy.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Acute uncomplicated cystitis – Likelihood: High
  - Suprapubic pain, frequency, and possible hematuria with mild constitutional symptoms support diagnosis; dysuria absent but not required.
- Urolithiasis (distal ureter or bladder stone) – Likelihood: Moderate
  - Pink urine and lower abdominal pain/frequency could fit; absence of colicky pain, flank pain, or radiation lowers probability.
- Early appendicitis – Likelihood: Moderate–Low
  - Gradual worsening lower abdominal pain with mild nausea and subjective feverishness; less typical due to midline/suprapubic localization and lack of migration or peritoneal signs.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Allergies not recorded.
  - Vitals and physical examination not performed/documented.
  - No urinalysis/urine culture obtained.
  - Pregnancy test pending.
  - Gynecologic ROS details (vaginal discharge/bleeding, dyspareunia) not fully explored.
  - Comprehensive medication list (including OTC/supplements) not reconciled.
  - Illicit drug use history not documented.
- Conflicts:
  - Patient name referred to as “Tim” and “Kim” (conflict noted).
  - Trimethoprim dosing instruction conflicting: “two tablets” versus “one tablet twice a day for three days” (clarification required).
  - LMP reported as “about three weeks ago” then “two weeks ago.”
- Transcript quality:
  - Minor stutters/pauses and some unclear fragments, but overall history understandable.
